## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ukkuṭika-sikkhāpada* constitutes the twenty-fifth training rule (*sekhiya*) of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates proper decorum regarding sitting in inhabited areas, specifically prohibiting squatting on the heels (*ukkuṭika*) [SuttaCentral]. A modern English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

This training rule is broadly attested across early Buddhist monastic traditions. In the Pali Vinaya, it corresponds directly to *sekhiya* 25 of the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and the *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Extensive cross-tradition parallels survive in both male and female monastic codes preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese translation, and Tibetan translation across diverse early Buddhist schools, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages [SuttaCentral].

Within the Pali canon, text-reuse analysis demonstrates extensive formulaic repetition across the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus records dozens of matching passages shared across 47 Pali texts, exhibiting particularly high textual overlap in introductory and framing formulas with adjacent rules such as Sekhiya 26 (sharing §0.1–1.9 with §0.1–1.15), Sekhiya 22, Sekhiya 24, Sekhiya 16, and Sekhiya 5 [DharmaNexus].
